speaker_notes.Joseph: Head Priest of WDT, Historian. Genuine strategic anguish over hard moral choices, protective worry, fond exasperation about a subordinate's overdue paperwork, repeated self-deprecating jabs at his own age and physical uselessness in dangerous places, dry indignation at political developments. Uses conversations with the Arisen as a way to think out loud.
speaker_notes.The White Dragon: The ancient dragon at the heart of Restania's covenant with its Arisen; weakened and slowly recovering strength, speaks in halting fragments while sensing distant threats and a rival dragon's movements; serves as mentor, judge, and moral compass to the Arisen, with real physical frailty visible beneath the authority
speaker_notes.Mephis: An undercover agent investigating a noble house; terse and businesslike on duty, warmer off duty. His stated mission is cover for personal revenge over a murdered mentor-figure, which he eventually admits to hiding; genuine gruff warmth and camaraderie toward the Arisen underneath (calls them "partner," admits he hasn't trusted anyone this much in years) without ever softening his blunt register.
speaker_notes.Barton: Innkeeper at the White Dragon Temple; warmly hospitable, quietly proud of his daughter
speaker_notes.Selin: A beauty salon stylist; sassy, playful, encouraging
speaker_notes.Orc Captain: An orc being interrogated; almost entirely roars and fragmented hostility
speaker_notes.Razanailt: Area Master of Farlana Plain; matriarch of a warrior village, wife of its chief. Warm, blunt, working-class dialect throughout, practical village-matriarch pride, protective loyalty once trust is earned ("no one in this village doubts you anymore -- you earned it with your own strength").
speaker_notes.Shalom: An attendant at a blessed hot spring; formally ceremonial
speaker_notes.Angelo: In charge of the festivals, excitable but slightly scheming; devoted to his girlfriend Shelly. Theatrical self-important bravado constantly undercut by genuine anxiety around impressing Shelly, comedic self-awareness about being "morale personnel, not combat personnel," running seasonal-event gags (Halloween, Valentine's, White Day) handled with real comic timing.
speaker_notes.Leo: Veteran Arisen, watches over and directs newer Arisen. Terse commands, protective mentorship delivered through orders rather than comfort, dry backhanded praise ("hah, you've gotten better"). Carries real unspoken guilt/care underneath a controlled exterior, especially regarding a fellow Arisen he feels responsible for -- handles it by taking the burden onto himself rather than talking it through.
speaker_notes.Mysial: A White Dragon Temple attendant, assists with pact ceremonies. Composed and reverent on the surface, real vulnerability breaking through in quiet moments ("forgive me, please forget I said that"). A lovely added dimension: a quiet daydream about what it would be like to be an ordinary 17-year-old girl, and secretly rooting for a woman she once saw asking her boyfriend for jewelry at the bazaar.
speaker_notes.Klaus: Junior archivist assisting a senior temple historian; earnest, anxious, curious. Constant mid-sentence self-correction and backtracking, apologetic over-explaining when asking favors, genuine anxious investment in the safety of people he cares about, openly doubts his own judgment rather than asserting conclusions.
speaker_notes.Elliot: A young soldier who idolizes his squad captain. Breathless combat energy, admiring devotion, repeatedly denies his own fear out loud ("I won't run, I really won't run!"). Real emotional weight comes through at key moments (heartbreak over a friend's fate, determination to survive) without ever losing the excitable, earnest core register.
speaker_notes.Ciarán: Area Master of a village in Kingaru Canyon; chieftain balancing tradition and change. Plainspoken, practical, formal "貴君" address, dignified worry about his village's fate, growing trust and gratitude toward the Arisen over an escalating series of crises.
speaker_notes.Vanessa: Fighter-vocation trainer; veteran frontline officer. Clipped commander tone, willing to admit her own strategic mistakes rather than deflect, deep protective worry about a fellow officer's unexplained absences. Shows reserved warmth rather than coldness when caught off guard by sentiment (visibly uncomfortable but genuinely touched by a gift).
speaker_notes.Lise: A young Arisen soldier, competitive and image-conscious. Breathless combat exclamations, genuine admiration of others' strength, occasional unexpected emotional insight beneath the excitable surface (crying without quite knowing why, noticing that people need to change themselves as well as be rescued).
speaker_notes.Alfred: An Area Master colleague; plain, practical. Plainspoken, formal "貴君" address, practical area-management exposition, growing trust and gratitude as the Arisen proves themselves.
speaker_notes.Christine: Area Master of the deep Misuriu forest; shrine keeper
speaker_notes.Dian: Area Master of the Zandra Forbidden Zone; a lost pawn whose Arisen died long ago, now serving the shrine
speaker_notes.Rondejeel: Area Master of the Dinan forest; researches lost elf lore alongside his sister
speaker_notes.Scherzo: Area Master of Bertrand Plains; fortress quartermaster
speaker_notes.Roy: Manager of the Kinoza hot springs and Area Master of the Bord mining district
speaker_notes.Beatrix: Area Master of Melgoda; alchemist survivor of a fallen kingdom
speaker_notes.Nadia: Area Master of Zoma; flirtatious frontier boss drawn to danger and ambition
speaker_notes.Sunny: Area Master of northern Bertrand region; innkeeper's wife, emotional and devoted to her hometown
speaker_notes.Bertrand: Captain of an island expedition team and its Area Master. Hearty commander energy, restrains himself from joining the front line out of duty despite wanting to ("this is exactly when my blood should be racing"), genuine warmth toward a personal old friend.
speaker_notes.Muirgel: Area Master of the Eran Suirin forest; caretaker hoping to rebuild a lost village. Elevated, graceful formal register throughout, warm gratitude, idealistic hope for restoration. A lovely added dimension: wistful awareness that once the village is fully restored, she'll have fewer reasons to ask the Arisen for help, and finds that quietly sad.
speaker_notes.Gurdolin: Veteran soldier craving excitement and battle; restless during quiet periods, secretly protective of those close to him. Crude blunt dialect throughout, recurring gambling/betting motif, protective battle-cries under a gruff exterior.
speaker_notes.Hayden: Area Master of Dow Valley (Jingen village); humble, deeply grateful village elder
speaker_notes.Sonel: Military strategist/tactician who thinks out loud constantly and openly acknowledges it; whimsically distractible (loses his own wand, forgets tasks mid-thought), delights in odd side-fixations (random objects brought to him get the same eager curiosity as military plans), comic spite when a substitute tool underperforms.
speaker_notes.Arthfael: Area Master of Moro Woodland (Morfort village); humble and grateful, protective of the forest. Deeply formal, humble, gratitude-heavy register throughout, ceremonial devotion to protecting his village and its spirit dragon.
speaker_notes.Gillian: A knight/guard from a foreign land who becomes a resistance/liberation army leader. Tests strangers before trusting them, but once earned, she is warm and direct: gives tactical leadership casually, states gratitude and loyalty outright rather than deflecting it, and works through a real emotional arc reconciling with her father's memory (misjudged him as a coward, learns he was brave, wants to apologize).
speaker_notes.O'Neill: Area Master of Bria Coast (Rotes village); laid-back, easily excitable about treasure and mysteries
speaker_notes.Mayleaf: A young girl living near the White Dragon Temple; innocent and emotionally open. Childlike simple sentences, constant pleading and worry for everyone around her. Sees herself as the future keeper of the story -- responsible for remembering and passing down everything that happens, which she takes with quiet, earnest seriousness beneath the innocence.
speaker_notes.Patricia: Area Master of the Misuriu forest (Lynwood village); competent, warmly businesslike
speaker_notes.Emerada: An unofficial Sorcerer mentor in the Misuriu forest; proud, teasing, haughty. Teasing, elegant, transactional-but-playful requests, affectionately watching the Arisen's growth with a mix of pride and playful reluctance ("my beautiful little bird, growing her feathers behind my back").
speaker_notes.Carrie: Runs the mess hall for a militia encampment; cheerful, energetic, nurtures the community (exclamatory warmth, playful tangents like naming rescued pigs). Her quest arc opens with real fear/self-doubt about leaving the fort that fades as she grows more confident -- worth knowing for early-arc lines specifically.
speaker_notes.Fabio: A fellow Arisen who deals in rare goods on the side; detached, dryly philosophical about fate and impermanence. Casual self-interested trading schemes, joking deflection, genuine guilt breaking through the detachment about the White Dragon's fall ("if I'd handled it better -- damn it"). NOTE: he's also the game's primary early-tutorial NPC -- a notable chunk of his dialogue is literal onboarding/UI instruction text, more so than most characters.
speaker_notes.Heinz: Vice-captain of a knight order; blunt, competitive pride in his knights. A bit envious of the Arisen's celebrity status among the knights, dry gossip about a fellow knight's petty gambling scandal, camaraderie mixed with grumbling about being stuck on guard duty while others get the glory.
speaker_notes.Meirova: An elderly general leading a knight order/resistance army; boisterous, proud, secretly protective of his granddaughter. Booming battle-cries, hearty festival laughter, fond exasperated cursing at Gillian for acting without him, real emotional depth at key moments (visibly overwhelmed reuniting with the prince he raised, admitting his words might not stop once they start).
speaker_notes.Bertha: An elderly master thief aiding a resistance effort; blunt, pragmatic, protective of her family. Warmly protective of the young prince despite constant grumbling that he's "still just a child," dry self-aware humor about her age and old thieving habits, weary wit about the city still distrusting her even after going legitimate.
speaker_notes.Ringdeel: A researcher preserving elf archery traditions in a forest; patient and warmly encouraging. Warm, patient, protective of the forest, quiet rueful pride watching the Arisen surpass her own skill ("a little annoying, honestly, but I should train harder too"), genuine warmth about having a training companion since she usually works alone.
speaker_notes.Adair Donnchadh: Master of spirit-lance combat at a training hall in Restania; stern, exacting, proud. Addresses others bluntly ("貴様") until they've earned otherwise. Reveals quiet care underneath the gruffness -- arranges discreet help for a talented young spearman he noticed struggling, calling it "a shame to let that talent go to waste."
speaker_notes.Gerhard: A loyal aide-officer serving under a general; formally polite, diplomatically composed
speaker_notes.Kirsty: The realm's Hyper-cutter (royal blade-master), served the former queen. Carries real unresolved guilt over choosing to evacuate civilians instead of fighting at her queen's side when she fell, replays the choice in her mind, and admits her life lost its meaning after the loss. Wit surfaces as a defensive social habit over that grief -- trailing silences, deflection from painful topics, quiet loneliness.
speaker_notes.Theodor: An alchemist mentor; thoughtful, composed, wrestling with the ethics of forbidden knowledge. Long analytical sentences explaining alchemy's history and mechanics, genuine intellectual wonder at ordinary objects from present-day Restania, dignified gratitude even under duress, tests the Arisen's readiness before granting new techniques.
speaker_notes.Cecily: A young woman searching for her lost memories and father. Opens vulnerable and apologetic after losing her memory, but grows into composed determination as her sense of purpose returns ("I have a mission," "hesitation is fatal"), genuine care for a troubled friend she is forced to fight, steady leadership organizing search efforts.
speaker_notes.Chester: A rope-and-dagger climbing specialist (Seeker); laid-back, adventure-loving, encouraging. Casual encouragement, competitive admiration of the Arisen's skill, playful self-satisfaction about his own speed and agility.
speaker_notes.Quintus: Garrison commander holding a fort for a resistance army; dry, self-deprecating, quietly hopeful. Plainspoken pragmatic leadership, dry self-deprecating asides about setting aside old grudges, real grief tempered with quiet acceptance over a lost friend ("that his family survived -- I'll count that as enough"), genuine warmth about hard-won victories.
speaker_notes.Nazik: Self-appointed interim Area Master of a war-torn region; humble, formally gracious. Deeply formal, humble, gratitude-heavy register throughout, including a reflective closing conversation looking back over the region's liberation.
speaker_notes.Nedo: A young prince displaced from his court; earnest, apologetic, eager to prove himself. Constant apologies, genuine self-doubt about his own inexperience ("not even close to being an Arisen, or fully a person"), touching frustration at his own limits, real growing determination and leadership taking shape underneath the humility.
speaker_notes.Oliver: Warrior-vocation trainer; a boisterous, over-the-top combat enthusiast. Constant maximum-intensity exclamation, combat treated as ecstatic experience, zero restraint even in routine instruction.
speaker_notes.Doris: Captain of a royal palace guard; composed, formally dutiful. Full formal keigo throughout, composed even reporting dire circumstances (her own captain missing, the capital fallen), stepping into command without losing her measured tone.
speaker_notes.Gerd: A knight order disciplinarian; blunt and rule-bound, secretly won over by the player's conduct. Formal address, staunch defense of the knight order's honor, real anguish over a betrayal by a trusted ally, a motivating backstory rooted in a past massacre that pushed him toward discipline and command, dry self-deprecating humor about his own scars, quiet dignity-preserving embarrassment when asking for discreet help.
speaker_notes.Luca: Guide of a cursed labyrinth dungeon; formally humble, businesslike about dungeon mechanics
speaker_notes.Bacias: Area Master of the mountain where the Fire Dragon once rested; humble, apologetic about past failures. Deeply formal, humble, gratitude-heavy register throughout, ceremonial devotion to the mountain's legacy and the royal family.
speaker_notes.Camus: Priest-vocation trainer at a temple; composed, philosophical about healing and mortality. Measured, philosophical about compassion and service ("to see the true nature of life -- that is what we Priests do"), respectful of privacy even when genuinely curious.
speaker_notes.Morgan: A guide connecting the Arisen to trials in a past version of Akkarshelan; formal, protective, encouraging
speaker_notes.Pehr: Sole guardian of a tomb dungeon; formally polite, protective, apologetic
speaker_notes.Ira: New recruit guarding a tomb dungeon; formally polite but visibly unsure of herself
speaker_notes.Selim: The spirit of a fallen general tied to a mountain shrine; solemn, wistful, encouraging
speaker_notes.Ivan: Hunter-vocation trainer; terse and economical, speaks in short practical bursts. Consistently fragmented, dropped-article speech throughout, genuine warmth and approval expressed tersely rather than through elaboration ("You -- everyone -- likes you"), protective of the forest and its creatures.
speaker_notes.Rudolfo: A retired knight-trainer now a lighthouse keeper; patient, warmly nostalgic mentor. Gentle elderly wisdom ("the sea is fair to everyone -- a good chance to reflect on oneself"), patient mentorship, warm gratitude toward the village that looks after him.
speaker_notes.Endale: Area Master of a mountainside garrison for a resistance army; blunt, practical, protective. Gruff and testing toward outsiders at first, dark humor about a past informant whose loose talk got the resistance killed, plainspoken and repeatedly grateful once trust is earned.
speaker_notes.Lisa: Adventurer's-notebook service clerk at the temple; cheerful, thorough, professionally warm
speaker_notes.Gearóid: An elder of a forest village facing a spreading blight, whose daughter is far from home; dignified, weighed down by guilt. Dignified restrained grief over his daughter's transformation into a corrupted spirit dragon ("even if her form has changed, may I still think of her as my daughter?"), steady dutiful leadership through an escalating sky-vortex crisis.
speaker_notes.Shelly: Girlfriend of a fellow festival enthusiast; bubbly, fashion-obsessed, romantic. Bubbly exclamatory event-hostess energy, devoted specifically to Angelo ("there's no one else for me"). Note: a Halloween storyline briefly has her speaking in broken, possessed-sounding katakana during a corruption/possession plot beat -- a temporary narrative device, not her normal register.
speaker_notes.Isel: The spirit of a royal archer bound to a ruined tower; dignified, wistful, quietly frustrated by her powerlessness
speaker_notes.Anita: A spirit bound to a shrine, once a formidable warrior; warm, casual, self-deprecating
speaker_notes.Lucien: Guide of a cursed labyrinth dungeon; formally humble
speaker_notes.Yuiato: The spirit of a former royal milk-brother tied to a coastal ruin; modest, warmly self-deprecating
speaker_notes.Maeve: Innkeeper running a village in her husband's stead; blunt, practical, no-nonsense
speaker_notes.Mordred: Chief's aide of a coastal village, standing in for its ailing chief; dignified, philosophically accepting
speaker_notes.Poe: Innkeeper at a ruin-town frequented by bandits and treasure hunters; boisterous, loves sharing local history
speaker_notes.Seneka: Keeper of the temple's public offering board and local news; cheerful, earnest, quietly anxious
speaker_notes.Actaeon: An alchemist inhabiting a strange timeless realm; composed, philosophical, quietly grateful
speaker_notes.Fulya: The spirit of a fallen kingdom's official; wistful and nostalgic for her country's former glory
speaker_notes.Zerkin: A ship captain running expeditions to a mysterious island; boisterous, romantic about the unknown sea
speaker_notes.Alan: A liaison at a frontier fort; casual, teasing, warmly admiring of his superior officer
speaker_notes.Emporio: An innkeeper in a struggling village, married to its Area Master; weary, self-deprecating, devoted
speaker_notes.Iris: A young, powerful fighter; breezy and playful on the surface, privately uneasy about right and wrong
speaker_notes.Gray: Village head of a struggling mountain settlement; weary, resigned, quietly caring
speaker_notes.Scylla: A temple attendant dispensing blessings and daily supplies; formally ceremonial
speaker_notes.Burj: Innkeeper of the oldest inn in a capital city; cheerful, exclamation-heavy hospitality
speaker_notes.Cameron: Attendant at a lottery/prize booth; bubbly, exclamation-heavy, admiring of lucky guests
speaker_notes.Damard: The spirit of a former royal swordsman guarding a tomb dungeon; dignified, formal
speaker_notes.Dirith: Assists her older sister (a forest researcher) at a modest inn; playful, eager to help, easily excitable
speaker_notes.Kemal: A guide for a war-torn region's tomb dungeon; formally humble, grieving over an orphaned young prince
speaker_notes.Maia: A guardian of a sleeping spirit dragon; formally devoted, protective
speaker_notes.Cornelia: A pawn bound to a fellow Arisen; stiffly formal, deadpan about her own nature
speaker_notes.Craig: A weapon-enhancement blacksmith at the temple; warmly earnest, self-deprecating about non-combat skills. Gave up personal combat glory years ago to dedicate himself to strengthening the whole Arisen corps through weapon-craft mastery, speaks of that choice with quiet conviction. Still genuinely self-deprecating about anything outside his craft -- sheepishly asks for design advice on a decorative request because he's "only ever made weapons."
speaker_notes.Gwenhwyfar: A guardian of a watchtower whose true purpose she won't fully explain; composed, dryly reserved
speaker_notes.Livian: Hot-springs innkeeper in a mining town; warm, generous, boisterous
speaker_notes.Lorna: A hunter helping rebuild a militia's mess hall; plainspoken, warm, quietly hopeful
speaker_notes.Parishard: An antique collector at a private clan hideout; whimsical, poetic about objects and their history
speaker_notes.Walt: Caretaker of a frontier fort; hearty, grateful, encouraging
speaker_notes.Federico: Caretaker of a village dealing with a spreading illness; reserved, practical, concerned
speaker_notes.Livia: A clan officer hopeful; bubbly, admiring of Arisen and knights
speaker_notes.Logan: A knight order officer skeptical of Arisen; blunt, duty-focused, occasionally reflective
speaker_notes.Lucas: A resistance fighter sheltering refugees near enemy lines; cautious, dutiful, quietly resolved
speaker_notes.Odran: A retired warrior managing a fort's rest facilities; hearty, encouraging
speaker_notes.Ophelia: A temple attendant dispensing revival blessings; formally ceremonial
speaker_notes.Talcott: A frontier fort soldier; blunt, terse, mildly bitter about his own limitations
speaker_notes.Archibald: A vocation-master combat trainer; plain, encouraging, duty-focused
speaker_notes.Clarissa: A disciplined field medic managing a temporary outpost; brisk, health-focused, no-nonsense
speaker_notes.Deirdre: A traveling temple attendant offering revival blessings; formally ceremonial, quietly resolute
speaker_notes.Felix: An inn manager with an eye for pretty faces, engaged to be married; casual, joking, devoted underneath
speaker_notes.Gas: Leader of a hidden refugee shelter; terse and economical, fiercely protective of those in his care
speaker_notes.Kibiza: A clan-services host at the tavern; warm, generous, thoughtfully hopeful
speaker_notes.Loeg: A displaced, reflective figure grappling with guilt over a past decision; gentle, nostalgic, melancholic
speaker_notes.Pamela: Caretaker of a grieving young girl who lost her clan; formally polite, quietly anxious on her behalf. Motherly worry runs through everything -- anxious about the girl's whereabouts, caring for a rotating cast of the sick and injured, quiet dignified stress as the crisis escalates around her household.
speaker_notes.Randolf: Innkeeper at a bandit hideout; gruff, blunt, deflects sentimentality
speaker_notes.Shekel: A refugee with medical training helping out despite her own injury; soft-spoken, apologetic, quietly capable
speaker_notes.Thea: A healer concerned with guests' emotional as well as physical wellbeing; warm, nurturing, gently teasing
speaker_notes.Alvar: Head of the Pawn Guild hub; dignified, philosophical about pawns and the nature of the Rift
speaker_notes.Barclay: An Area Master's colleague managing village affairs; plain, practical
speaker_notes.Bruno: An innkeeper caring for war-weary refugees; warmly encouraging despite hardship
speaker_notes.Harold: Innkeeper of a fishing village's tavern; cheerful, exclamation-heavy hospitality
speaker_notes.Ingrid: Innkeeper in a lakeside village; warm, gently teasing hospitality
speaker_notes.Joaquim: A bandit managing a hideout's shelter; gruff, plainspoken
speaker_notes.Metrophanes: An alchemist wracked with guilt over forbidden research; dignified, sorrowful
speaker_notes.Nicola: A pawn serving at the Pawn Sanctuary; formally humble, devoted
speaker_notes.Seabell: A traveling bard; theatrical, exclamation-heavy, romantic about heroic tales
speaker_notes.Youssef: Leader of a desert outpost haunted by a past failure to defend a city; formally composed, guilt-driven
speaker_notes.Ellen: A young shop clerk; earnest, soft-spoken, quietly anxious about the state of the world
speaker_notes.Freud: A village watchman; earnest but insecure about his own capabilities
speaker_notes.Gregory: An appraisal-trading merchant; sly, ingratiating, business-savvy
speaker_notes.Hancock: A young guard watching over a mysterious ruin; eager, dutiful, enthusiastic
speaker_notes.Kieshildt: A cryptic, riddle-speaking figure who reflects on morality and perception; gentle, watchful, enigmatic
speaker_notes.Travers: A knight recruit-trainer loyal to his order's captain; blunt, duty-focused
speaker_notes.Axel: A priest assisting at a border encampment; casual, self-deprecating, easygoing about orders
speaker_notes.Brad: A former battlefield wanderer who's found comfort helping at a mess hall; warm, quietly content
speaker_notes.Dingus: An innkeeper and combat-technique trainer; calm, humble, patient
speaker_notes.Sunika: A bandit devoted to the cook who runs the mess hall; warmly loyal, quirky about footwear. Thief-dialect speech, deep loyalty to "Carrie the boss lady," humble self-deprecating humor about his own mishaps (sprains his ankle chasing a "phantom ingredient," traps the wrong thing in his own snare).
speaker_notes.Ariadne: A spirit-trader homesick for the surface world she can no longer visit; formal, wistful
speaker_notes.Diamantes: A rival alchemist bent on destroying and remaking the world; cold, resolute, contemptuous
speaker_notes.Dikka: A frontier scout who tracks local dangers; chatty, gossipy, self-deprecating about his own bad luck
speaker_notes.Gort: A villager who lost loved ones to orc raids; weary, dignified, stubbornly hopeful
speaker_notes.Mogok: A hostile enemy commander; cold, contemptuous, openly murderous
speaker_notes.Black Knight: A hostile armored antagonist; cold, dismissive, threatening
speaker_notes.Garrulous Skeleton: An undead commander tired of babysitting weaker monsters; comedic, self-aware, put-upon
speaker_notes.Pascal: A minor spirit guiding passage through a shrine full of collected souls; casual, friendly
speaker_notes.Pisarr: Chief of a warrior village; proud, stern but fair, protective of his people
speaker_notes.Sonia: A pawn attendant at the crafting room; formally humble, devoted
speaker_notes.Zuhl: A monster commanding other monsters (orcs, etc.) as underlings; gleeful, unpredictable, delights in violence
speaker_notes.Adelin: A young girl kept close to home by her mother, curious about the outside world; innocent, wistful
speaker_notes.Adem: A very young boy, frightened and looking for his mother; innocent, simple
speaker_notes.Alkane: A villager sharing local lore and hazards; warm, plainspoken, helpful
speaker_notes.Boadicea: An anxious village matriarch wary of change or danger; nervous, risk-averse
speaker_notes.Colette: A weapons shop owner; cheerful, upbeat, businesslike
speaker_notes.Dennis: A young boy separated from his family; scared but hopeful, simple
speaker_notes.Eugene: A traveling merchant dealing in materials; dry, practical, resigned to competition
speaker_notes.Hilde: A gossipy villager eager for news and rumors; elevated speech, chatty, nervously excitable
speaker_notes.Iosef: A person from a group displaced in a strange, timeless otherworld, now endangered by an alchemist's magical constructs; weary, philosophically resigned, homesick
speaker_notes.Isaac: A researcher-turned-quest-giver in Restania. Casual, wry, self-deprecating register day to day -- dry humor about chores he gets stuck with, playful deflection ("who would I give it to? -- turn that around, who do you think?"), casual camaraderie building over time. Retains a habit of turning direct questions back on the listener rather than answering. Rare serious moments (an existential crisis about his purpose, major plot beats) show real gravitas underneath the casual surface.
speaker_notes.Josephine: Adem's mother, whose home was destroyed; initially guarded, fiercely protective, quietly resolved to rebuild
speaker_notes.Josh: A checkpoint guard restricting access to a dangerous valley; formal, duty-focused
speaker_notes.Luchino: A costumed festival worker, laid-back and easygoing; casually affectionate toward his girlfriend
speaker_notes.Lucy: An attendant at a hot springs; warmly informative, service-oriented
speaker_notes.Marisa: A costumed festival worker, dating a coworker; breezy, carefree
speaker_notes.Muge: A soldier stationed at a besieged capital. Casual, giggly, gossipy energy throughout, genuine fear when she stumbles into real danger, and a tsundere-flavored testing of the Arisen's strength ("not like I want you to protect me or anything!").
speaker_notes.Oengus: A superstitious villager fearful of a nearby ruin; anxious, prone to catastrophizing
speaker_notes.Orhan: A guarded, embittered figure who refuses to hope to protect himself from disappointment; cynical, defensive
speaker_notes.Renton: A new knight recruit; casual, laid-back, easily distracted by fun. Casual, encouraging trainer energy, genuinely moved watching the Arisen grow ("it really gets me, right here"), shy blush receiving a gift.
speaker_notes.Riagan: A retired warrior of a warrior village; stern, testing others' worth before trusting them
speaker_notes.Sally: A food-ingredients shop clerk; cheerful, informative
speaker_notes.Sonya: A swordswoman seeking to become a master's apprentice; dignified, focused, prickly when her intentions are questioned
speaker_notes.Suleiman: A human blacksmith competing with pawn craftsmanship; boisterous, proud, hearty
speaker_notes.Aidan: A soldier helping restore a militia's mess hall; warm, encouraging, nostalgic for happier times
speaker_notes.Carlotta: A refugee soldier grieving for her family; withdrawn, exhausted, quietly grieving
speaker_notes.Charleston: Publisher of a local newspaper; proud of informing the public, modestly aware of his limits
speaker_notes.Duke: An officer at a knight order's command post; blunt, admits his own short temper
speaker_notes.Eddys: A wounded soldier slow to heal; dignified, stoic, quietly wistful about the world's troubles
speaker_notes.Erdogan: A proud, long-established shopkeeper; boastful, business-savvy, dismissive of rivals
speaker_notes.Flavell: A shopkeeper waiting for her partner's return from treasure-hunting; wistful, hopeful, quietly worried
speaker_notes.Ginette: A soldier displaced from her home region; anxious, uncertain, seeking reassurance
speaker_notes.Gordon: A villager frustrated by recurring goblin problems; blunt, grumbling
speaker_notes.Ivey: A civilian living amid crisis; frightened but finds comfort in the Arisen's presence
speaker_notes.Jan: A civilian earning back the community's trust; defensive, prideful, protective of a child in his care. A reformed thief who joins the Resistance against a corrupt marquis, working alongside Mephis; blunt working-class dialect, prideful about his own code ("I don't steal outside of work"), growing genuine investment in the cause once given real purpose ("I've been living for this day").
speaker_notes.Johann: A villager sharing local rumors; timid, apologetic about his own lack of courage
speaker_notes.Jonas: A soldier guarding a remote checkpoint; duty-focused, switches between formal and casual tone
speaker_notes.Karen: A tavern keeper comforting frightened patrons amid crisis; warm, reassuring
speaker_notes.Information Dealer: A streetwise hustler running several small trades; dry, pragmatic, self-aware about her marginalized status
speaker_notes.Kenan: A rescued torture survivor recovering in a reclaimed castle; frail, apologetic, quietly hopeful
speaker_notes.Lara: A tavern singer in a death-haunted village; world-weary, matter-of-fact about danger
speaker_notes.Linus: An elderly resident of the war-torn capital; humble, self-effacing, worried for the city's youth
speaker_notes.Mavail: A young villager restless under travel restrictions; warm, protective of his family
speaker_notes.Meriem: A young bazaar clerk raising her little brother alone; quietly self-sacrificing, caring
speaker_notes.Nave: A village elder enforcing local taboos against outsiders; stern, curt, dogmatic
speaker_notes.Tadhg: A guardian keeping watch over a spirit dragon shrine; composed, dutiful, reluctant to discuss the crisis
speaker_notes.Thales: An aging fisherman still working despite growing dangers at sea; weary but resilient, grumbling
speaker_notes.Aesop: A lounge singer at a hot springs resort; flamboyant, theatrical, self-promoting
speaker_notes.Cedric: An elderly villager who shares old adventure stories; warm, a little worried about his grandchild
speaker_notes.Cemil: A bazaar trader; casual, chatty, deflects fear with humor and practicality

speaker_notes.Navid: Marquis Navid Kurt, ruler of Megado -- gracious, formally polite host whose courtesy is a deliberate mask over real corruption (secret dealings with orcs, embezzlement, framing the Resistance, manipulating the Arisen). Revealed to be connected to Mephis's backstory as the one responsible for his mentor's death.

speaker_notes.Necro Master: A corpse-collecting necromancer with garbled, broken speech; menacing, monstrous
speaker_notes.Knight of the White Guard Order: SHARED LABEL, not one character -- covers at least 6-8 distinct one-off quest-giver knights (escort duty, cave investigation, siege defense, monster-hunt commander, squatter dispute, training-shrine gatekeeper, room-construction work). Register is consistently formal-and-duty-bound across nearly all instances (same family as Leo/Heinz), so E is given as a reasonable fallback -- but individual instances carry real personality color (embarrassment, wry self-awareness, gratitude) that this shared label flattens. Treat as a default, not a specific voice.
speaker_notes.Lightly-Equipped Soldier: SHARED LABEL, not one character -- covers several distinct one-off quest-givers (a smuggler wanting cellar goods retrieved, a checkpoint-blocked runner, someone panicked about approaching monsters). Register is consistently blunt and casual ("aze/ya" dialect) across instances, same family as Gurdolin/Bertha, so B is given as a fallback. Treat as a default, not a specific voice.
speaker_notes.Hunter: SHARED LABEL, not one character -- covers multiple different treasure-hunter/researcher quest-givers across different ruins. Register is consistently casual, scheming, and self-interested (using the Arisen for profit or safety), same family as Rick/Anerian, so F is given as a fallback. Treat as a default, not a specific voice.
speaker_notes.Soldier: SHARED LABEL, not one character -- covers multiple different one-off quest-givers (mountain-path monster hunt, a soldier who lost recovered treasure and is ashamed to report it). Register is consistently blunt and casual ("antaa" address), same family as Gurdolin, so B is given as a fallback. Treat as a default, not a specific voice.
speaker_notes.Rothgill Soldier: SHARED LABEL, not one character -- small set (9 lines) covering 2-3 soldiers in one battle scene (a wounded messenger, others acknowledging the situation). Register is consistent -- dutiful, urgent, grateful -- so E is given as a reasonable fallback.
speaker_notes.Liberation Army Soldier: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and NO single fallback archetype recommended -- genuinely heterogeneous. Covers casual frontline soldiers (blunt, personal, E/B-like) alongside distinct formal-report deliverers (polite, informational, closer to T). Forcing one archetype would mislead for roughly half the instances. Recommend defaulting to neutral house style (no archetype tag) for lines under this label unless the pipeline can distinguish specific quest/instance.
speaker_notes.Megado Guard: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and NO single fallback archetype recommended -- genuinely heterogeneous. Covers a starstruck young recruit (eager, flustered, C3-like), a composed formal report-giving veteran (T-like), and gossiping bystanders. Also contains unresolved placeholder tags (e.g. <NPC 681>) in the raw text -- a data cleanliness issue worth flagging to whoever owns the export, separate from the personality question. Recommend defaulting to neutral house style unless the pipeline can distinguish specific instances.
speaker_notes.Military Police: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and NO single fallback archetype recommended -- genuinely heterogeneous, and notably wider-ranging than most pooled labels: includes an arrogant, power-tripping bully (H-adjacent), a nervous junior officer, formal duty-focused pursuit dialogue (E-like), and a wistful officer reflecting on a fallen former colleague (A3-like). Recommend defaulting to neutral house style unless the pipeline can distinguish specific instances -- applying any single archetype here risks misrepresenting the corrupt-cop lines especially.
speaker_notes.Arisen Corps Regimental Soldier: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and NO single fallback archetype recommended -- by far the largest and most heterogeneous pool found (254 unique lines out of 307), spanning casual banter, formal acknowledgment, personal grumbling, and gratitude. IMPORTANT: sampling across the full range turned up at least one line that is pure gameplay/tutorial instruction text ("head to the back of the shrine and defeat the enemy there with combo attacks or sunder strikes -- don't forget to guard") attributed to this same character label. This confirms the concern about tutorial/system text being mixed into character-labeled dialogue -- worth a broader check across the file for other instances of this before this data feeds a translation pipeline. Recommend defaulting to neutral house style unless the pipeline can distinguish specific instances, and filtering obvious instructional text separately from character voice work entirely.

speaker_notes.Thug: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and too thin/mixed for a fallback -- only 8 lines split between a cocky quest-giver, an unrelated nervous newcomer, and a hostile one-off outburst. speaker_notes.Sorcerer: SHARED LABEL covering at least three unrelated things: (1) a male researcher investigating a forbidden-technique laboratory (curious, eager, C4/O-adjacent), (2) an unrelated formal female bell-delivery quest-giver (T/L-adjacent), and (3) a chunk of PURE SORCERER-VOCATION TUTORIAL TEXT with literal button-prompt tags (<COL><KCT> etc.) and "Tutorial Guide" references -- same non-dialogue issue found under "Priest". No archetype assigned; recommend neutral house style plus filtering the tutorial portion out entirely before any translation work.
speaker_notes.Man: SHARED LABEL, not one character, and NO single fallback archetype recommended -- heterogeneous. speaker_notes.Priest: Confirmed PURE TUTORIAL/UI TEXT, not character dialogue at all -- literal button-prompt tags (<COL ff7575><KCT ATTACK2></COL>), skill names, and explicit references to "the Tutorial Guide". speaker_notes.Little Flower: A Mandragora (magical plant creature) being coaxed/tamed; entirely non-verbal squeaks with narrator-description brackets (e.g. "[Mandragora shows defiance]"). No archetype assigned -- not enough spoken content to support one.
speaker_notes.War Master: Only 1 line ("You there! I'll return the wound I took at the watchtower!"), below the usable threshold. No archetype assigned.
